q-42255.name: Question 1
q-42255.problem:
Let $V=C[-\frac{\pi }{2},0],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[-\frac{\pi }{2},0].$ Find $⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
q-42255.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can evaluate this integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{{u}^{3}}{3}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[-\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}]-[-\frac{(0)^{3}}{3}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-42256.name: Question 2
q-42256.problem:
Let $V=C[0,2],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2].$ Find $⟨t,{e}^{t}⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
q-42256.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨t,{e}^{t}⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We denote

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⟹ & {u}^{′}=1, \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{t} & ⟹ & v=\int {v}^{′}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t={e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for the integration by parts, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =uv{|}_{0}^{2}-{\int }_{0}^{2}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t{e}^{t}){|}_{0}^{2}-{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(2{e}^{2}-0{e}^{0})-{e}^{t}{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2{e}^{2}-({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-43813.name: Question 3
q-43813.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2$, equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Find $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$, if

$$
x(t)=3+t-2{t}^{2},\,y(t)=t-3.
$$
q-43813.worked_solution:
Computing the inner product according to the definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =x(0)y(0)+x(-1)y(-1)+x(2)y(2) \\  & =3\cdot (-3)+0\cdot (-4)+(-3)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-9+0+3 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

q-76450.name: Question 5
q-76450.problem:
Let $V=C[0,2\pi ],$ the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2\pi ].$ Find $⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)⟩$ if the inner product on $V$ is defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the identity $\operatorname{cos}⁡\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡\beta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha -\beta )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha +\beta )).$*
q-76450.worked_solution:
We need to evaluate

$$
⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can evaluate this integral using the identity $\operatorname{cos}⁡\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡\beta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha -\beta )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha +\beta ))$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-4t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(6t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(6t)}{6}){|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\pi )}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(12\pi )}{6}]-\frac{1}{2}[-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0}{6}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
